scope: Read-only code review of the frozen v5 files listed in input_manifest.json. I read the manifest, code_v4_review.json, pesuqei.py, the pesuqei test file, morning_shared.py, morning_witnesses.py, authoring.py, test.log and junit.xml. I did not open the spines, the YAML profiles, JLPTEI-3.md or SCAN_DIGITIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS.md, because they are source/recipe/export material. opensiddur.exporter.urn.split_range was not supplied, so I did not read it. I ran nothing, edited nothing and hashed nothing. Every hash below is copied from the manifest or test.log. This approval covers code only; it is not a source, recipe or export approval.

binding.results: test.log:100 reports 76 passed and 31 subtests passed. junit.xml has tests=107 with errors=0, failures=0 and skipped=0, which equals 76+31. The pesuqei test IDs are at test.log:69-94 and include the new test_range_availability_must_match_actual_witness_boundaries.

evidence: pesuqei.py:198-212 runs after apply_corrections. apply_corrections changes the same root objects in place (authoring.py:268-279), so by_path sees the corrected trees. The check also runs before any guard, service document or spine is built.

Line 202 gets the endpoints from the shared split_range, or uses the single target if the span is not a range. Lines 203-207 work out which of the unit's languages actually have every endpoint as an @corresp on some element of the generated document, including the root. If that set differs from set(span.witnesses), the build fails.

Lines 208-212: when 'en' is not in witnesses, any element in any in-batch English document whose @corresp is an endpoint fails the build. This covers other units' documents too, not just the span's own unit.

Fail-closed note: witnesses cannot be empty (line 188). So if split_range returned endpoints in an unexpected form, the actual set would come out empty, the comparison would fail and the build would raise. It would not pass silently.

Tests at test:438-450 cover both directions. In 'unprinted_english', the English reading carries v2 while witnesses is ['he'], and the build raises. In 'missing_english', witnesses is ['he','en'] but the English corresp has been moved, and the build raises. Both assert the message 'availability disagrees'.

The existing-file gate (pesuqei.py:275-286) uses root.iter(), so it checks every element including the root. Its target set is the repeat targets plus every span target without 'en'. Regenerated paths are exempt. It runs at main:331, after build_documents and before verify_existing_outputs and write_documents.
The in-batch gate (pesuqei.py:216-226) counts every English element of any type whose @corresp equals the target. It requires exactly one match, and that match must be a tei:milestone.
Regressions at test:401-419 cover the milestone provider, the regenerated-path exemption and the synthetic old root div/@corresp provider.

Each item.ranges span gets its own canonical call. Expanded mode calls every span, unqualified (pesuqei.py:168-170). Documentary mode calls a language only if it is listed in span.witnesses (106-109). A language the unit does not have is skipped earlier (101-102).

build_documents rejects repeat combined with ranges (185-186), and empty witnesses or witnesses outside the unit's languages (187-189). It sends every span target through call(), which rejects qualified and non-text URNs before anything is built (190).

Generated E2E (test:320-399): psalms/8/2 is Hebrew only and sits between bilingual verses 1 and 3. It runs alongside the HE×2/EN×1 repeat and the unselected-English fallback. For both the expanded spine and the documentary Hebrew service it checks: each PARTn-he appears once; PART2-en is absent while PART1-en and PART3-en appear once each; the v2 transclusion appears once and its parallel counterpart is empty; and the English page changes are exactly n7, n8, n9, so the Hebrew-only verse adds no English page. These are documents actually generated by build_documents, indexed in refdb and compiled with ExternalCompilerProcessor.

findings.detail: The guards do not fully cover multi-verse Hebrew-only spans. The in-batch gate (208-212) checks only the two endpoints, so an English provider for an interior verse would pass. The existing-file gate (278-279, 285) compares @corresp to the raw span target string. For a range target such as .../8/2-4, an older English provider for v2, v3 or v4 would not be caught. This is not exposed when every span without 'en' is a single verse, which is the only case the tests cover.
findings.required_for: Recipe approval must confirm that every span without 'en' is a single verse. Otherwise the code needs to expand these targets to all their verses in both gates before such a recipe is used.

findings.detail: Some paths are correct by reading but not tested. (a) The cross-document check at 208-212, 'would fill an untranslated range', is never reached on its own, because both R1 tests are caught first by the equality check. (b) Nothing exercises an in-batch non-milestone repeat provider. (c) The English documentary service calls (v1 and v3 @en, no v2) are not checked directly. They are covered only indirectly, through parallel compilation.

There are still no tests for repeat+range rejection, the witness-subset or empty-witness rejection, or a qualified range target. Spans are not checked to fall inside the unit, to be in order, to be free of overlap, or to be unique. In expanded mode expanded_target is silently ignored when ranges are present. These belong to recipe review.

prior_findings: N1, N3-N7 and F1-F14 stay closed as in v3/v4, and their low residuals carry over: registry acceptance and j:conditional placement not read; the day-one Hebrew transclusion fallback; baseline_commit only checked as 40 hex characters; the exact-match limit for providers through a containing unit.
